steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Marcin, how come this place feels so darn quiet lately?

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: You think? Maybe it only feels that way because you have one less person to talk to, now that Maria's no longer around.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Now that you mention it, I guess that might be it.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: I mean, at her age, should really should go out and see the world. It's just, who knows when she'll remember to come home for a visit?

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: You'd better get everything in your workshop in order then, old bones. When she finally gets back, you should hand her the keys.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Ah, it's been a while, my favorite customer.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Good afternoon, everybody.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Looks like the Radiant Knight can finally catch a breather?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Everything is starting to move in the right direction, and I'm getting used to handling the desk work.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: I've been saying this for some time now, but don't try to take on everything. Now that Zofia and Maria aren't around, how are you supposed to deal with all this?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Yeah, thanks for worrying about me. It's true that there is much I can't handle. All I can do is deal with what I can.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Perhaps it's because I've been away from Kazimierz for too long, or perhaps I just never knew much about the city's rules in the first place.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: And now that I must live with these rules for the foreseeable future, I finally realize how little I understood.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Sometimes, I even think that... From what I remember of my time in Kazimierz before my exile, all I ever did was take Grandfather's hand, follow him, and watch the scenery from that safe road.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: If I may ask once again, what happened during the years I was away?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Ah, what a coincidence. Fancy running into you again, Sir Młynar.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You commissioned the bounty hunters and disappeared just as quickly. That kind of behavior gets you blacklisted, you know.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...Do you need something?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Me? I'm just here to take a look at the village. After all, the villagers did send us a message asking for help.

spans.text: Me? I'm just here to take a look at the village. After all, the villagers
send us a message asking for help.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The construction team was supposed to start work today, but now that Gale Industries is under investigation, the land sale has been called off. Or so I hear.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I do read the papers.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Oh, then I'm sure you've also read that the investigation dragged in quite a number of other companies and old noble families. The National Council even dug up a certain old case from a few years ago, all thanks to this.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The ones who took the blame back then are long gone, and not a lot of people still remember how it all went down.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But I'm sure you do?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If they're no longer around, is there really a point in celebrating this?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I suppose you're right. I'm sure our good noble knight wouldn't consider those men even worth taking revenge on.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: As for us lowly bounty hunters... All we did is help pass the evidence from one pair of hands to another. Nothing worth paying any mind to.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But now that everything's been taken care of and the dust has settled... We go pretty far back, right? I think I've earned the right to ask a few questions?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If it's about Czcibor, I have nothing to say.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Right... I think we both need some time to ourselves. If you still need to mull this over, I shan't bother you.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But I'm sure you know how I managed to find you.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: All I'm saying is... I have nothing to say.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If you're really that curious... He was an unwavering man who rambled on about his impossible ideals for the knighthood, right to the very end.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: And if you think this deserves mourning... suit yourself.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hah, from the sounds of it, that was quite the cruel final conversation.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But since you brought it up, I suppose it's not so bad to talk about it a little.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I remember there was this one time I ran into that self-taught medic of ours. He was with a heavily injured comrade of his, lying on the ground. So he picked up a weapon and sent his friend on his way.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I have no idea what they talked about. All I could see was that he was covered in blood and looked pretty uncomfortable. He must have been depressed, or so I thought.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But do you know what he said after that?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: He told me the blood was too hot.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It might actually be a pretty nice way to go, thinking everything's looking hopeful and that your ideals are about to come true.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Alas, if at the very end you're still only talking ideals, you probably aren't dying with your mind at ease. You could still probably make everyone else feel burnt, though.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Burnt?...Given the biased ideals he chose in his depression and anger, I have no sympathy for a tragic end.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: His doubts don't even compare to everything I've pondered over the years.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: If you wanted to find out what drove him to such extremes, be it pain or ambition, then I'm afraid you'll be disappointed.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Really? What a shame.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Surely you've seen enough men stray onto the wrong path?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A few years back, we had a small skirmish with another band of hunters in this area. He lent us a helping hand. Or rather, he chased away both sides.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: A campaign knight who'd choose to go on patrol all over the place on his own... Quite interesting, wouldn't you agree? At the very least, I'd say he was a stronger man than a certain noble scion who was working an office job in the Grand Knight Territory.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: This isn't the time for your jokes, Toland.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hah, don't be so serious.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I even heard that, after this whole conspiracy was exposed, some of the Infected workmen were given protection in secret, sparing them from becoming needless sacrifices in the political struggle's aftermath.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: —And well, I found you through them.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: What do you think now, Młynar?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: It's been years.

a.text: A knight should not remain forever in doubt. He should have an answer that he firmly believes in.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I've never had an answer.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Kazimierz does not need an answer from me, either.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: I'm an ordinary man, nothing more. Why ask me?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Then perhaps... you should think about doing something other than holing yourself up in the Grand Knight Territory again.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You can't keep blaming yourself for his death, much less go this far to atone for it.

steps.name: Eager Bartender
steps.text: —Excuse me, are you two tourists?

steps.name: Eager Bartender
steps.text: Our beer is known far and wide, so would each of you like to try a pint? You may, of course, drink outside if you'd like.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: No thanks. Weather's getting cold.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...Too bad. I only turned her down because of how dreary drinking by myself would be. Otherwise, I could really use some booze to lighten things up.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: If only Czcibor had behaved himself for just a couple more days, we could've had a blast at our reunion party.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: That way, you could've kept a clear head and stayed out of it. No one would've blamed you for it.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I never said I'd stand aside and do nothing.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: However, I was the one who refuted his ideals. I listened to him until the very end...

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...and I killed him.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: But I... I respect his life nonetheless. If only for his final question and nothing more, I must find an answer.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I visited Grandfather's grave this morning.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I thought about a lot of things as I stood there. My regrets about the past... and for certain things in the present.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I really wish I could still talk to him, tell him about all this, seek his advice, but all I could do was say my farewells after such a long absence.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...It hadn't sunk in until after I'd finished all my work last night and set down my pen. He truly isn't with us anymore. I didn't have to keep my voice down so as not to disturb him.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Gah, don't blame yourself, Margaret.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: We all know you couldn't have made it back, nor should you have.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Nonetheless, I still feel terrible for not being able to stay by my grandfather's side, or to hear his final wishes.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...Maria told me that he sent a Messenger for me from his deathbed.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Huh. Now that you mention it, yeah.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: But Kirill seemed even happier when the Messenger told him she couldn't reach you. After all, if a Messenger can't find you, then an assassin sure as hell can't.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: He told us himself that he'd rather the children of the Nearl family grow up elsewhere, instead of Kazimierz as it is now.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: At the very least, I'm sure he'd be more than satisfied if he could see you now.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: So, how was the family after Grandfather passed away?

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Not gonna lie, some folks still have it out for the Nearls. Even the Messenger he sent after you got shot by an arrow not long after she got back. She had to hide out here for a while.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: *Spit*. Just a bunch of cowards who've only got the balls to ambush a Messenger. If someone really dared to pick a fight with the Nearls, we wouldn't just sit on the sidelines and watch.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I should've realized sooner that this sort of thing could happen. Only Grandfather's reputation was shielding us from these attacks, covert and otherwise.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Actually, I was threatened too, not long ago.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Who's got the balls to pick a fight with you?!

spans.text: Who's got the balls to pick a fight with

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Oh, no, not me directly. A friend that I had recently met at a welfare event was injured. I only found out afterward.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Apparently my speech offended some members of the G.C.C. They sent an anonymous letter warning me to be more careful about what I say.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: But I understand that this didn't happen because of a single speech or turn of phrase. It's more likely that they simply used that as an excuse.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Perhaps such attacks will happen again and again, until I'm made to cower and stop being a thorn in their side.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Of course, I don't plan to let that happen. I will keep fighting, and do everything in my power to protect others. I just thought you should know.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: It's just like the Major. It's only thanks to the support of my friends that I could finish the competition.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Eh, why even mention it? Can't we at least help the Nearls out in their time of need? Besides, not a single one of the folks that came looking for trouble knew how to fight if their lives depended on it.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Don't forget to come to us for help just because you're too busy with work.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Thanks for always being there for us, everyone.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Aw, our little Margaret is starting to act more and more like a real Knight Primus.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: No, I've only just gotten back to Kazimierz. There are still so many responsibilities I must shoulder, but don't fully understand.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Right, Margaret, you're Rhodes Island's liaison with Kazimierz. They take care of quite a few Infected, don't they?

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Are the Infected and medical personnel there part of those responsibilities too?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Oh, there is nothing to worry about on that end. Rhodes Island has attempted aid in places where their status is even more complicated than it is here. They know how to navigate these societal pitfalls much better than me.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: That said... There are quite a lot of Infected who don't want to go through with the treatment, and that's actually our biggest problem.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Hm... Because of money?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Right. The emergency treatment that they provide is only temporary. To continue to suppress the Oripathy's growth, you have to keep buying medicine in the long term.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: The way Kazimierz is now, there's no path for the Infected other than becoming a knight. Some will never be able to afford the cost of ongoing treatment.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: There are also many who think Rhodes Island is just trying to squeeze money out of them. After all, it is an incurable disease.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: —Sorry for rambling, I always get carried away whenever I talk about the Infected.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Well, you've got no one to vent to at home. If you need someone to talk to, you could do worse than us.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Besides, hearing you worry about all that stuff really brings it home that you're an adult now.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Haha... Master Kowal, do you remember my parents' portrait we have in the hall at home? The one from their younger years?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I only noticed this just yesterday, but I look almost the same age now as they do in that painting.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Hah? Well, when you put it that way, time sure has flown by.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Right, I feel the same, and that's one of the reasons why I wanted to stop by today.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I remember back when my parents had just left. I had just learned to read well enough to take in a whole novel.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Back then, looking at the illustrations in those knightly legends, I always thought the female leads were drawn based on Mother.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: But what kind of knights were they, anyway? When they left, I wasn't even old enough to seriously spar with Father in the training grounds.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: And once, during a duel, Uncle Liam told me I resembled my father...

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: That punk Schnitz, huh...?

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Back when I was still a campaign knight, I'd never seen a young man better suited for the word 'talented.'

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Even setting aside being Kirill's oldest son, he was unstoppable. Legends about him were already spreading like wildfire when he was still a squire...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Sorry, I have a phone call.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...Negotiate which occasions call for deploying the Infected diagnosis technology? Very well, I'll pass it on and make the preparations.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: Sounds like the Radiant Knight is busy.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: I'm sorry. I was hoping to stay a little longer.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Go on now. Us old folks aren't going anywhere.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Hmph, I'm still thinking about the Nearls. It's been a while since anyone's mentioned Schnitz.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: It's too bad. He could've gone down in Kazimierzian history as a hero like his father. Hell, he should've.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Right. I just never thought a bright light like his would turn out to be a brief spark on the battlefield.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Remember how we were launching a counterattack on the fortress at the easternmost point of the battlefront? And there was a squad that cut off Ursus's first wave of reinforcements?

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: Hah, how could I forget? Back then, I really thought the two of them would stand side-by-side on the battlefield as leaders of the campaign knights in only a few more years.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: I remember I was planning on sticking around until both the Nearl young'uns had made a name for themselves.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Who would've thought that by the time we finally left the battlefield, there wouldn't be any Nearls in the campaign knights.

spans.text: Who would've thought that by the time we finally left the battlefield, there wouldn't be

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: *Sigh*... And that punk Młynar left of his own volition.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Well, it's not like he led a real knightclub.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Schnitz wanted to include them in the operation, but the other knightclubs pushed back, and Młynar just didn't want his friends bullied.

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: ...'How could a bunch of refugees who simply want to break through the fortress and return to their homelands possibly compare to us knights?'

steps.name: Old Knight
steps.text: Speaking of, where did that punk run off to? I should've asked Margaret just now.

steps.name: Bald Marcin
steps.text: If she didn't bring it up, he probably hasn't written back yet.

steps.name: Old Craftsman
steps.text: He used to leave home for months or years at a time, didn't he? Don't worry about him. Margaret's here to take care of the family. Things'll get better, slowly but surely.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: ...I won't ask what you two talked about in the end.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: You made your decision.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But if you told me that there's no longer a place for knights in Kazimierz, I suppose I wouldn't disagree.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The vast majority of folks prefer the performers in the arenas, who can help them forget their hardships, over a knight who can actually shatter their suffering.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I mean, they don't actually want to see their lives shattered. It's a waste of time and effort. Besides, putting up a struggle till the very end rarely ends well.

spans.text: to see their lives shattered. It's a waste of time and effort. Besides, putting up a struggle till the very end rarely ends well.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...He understood that, no doubt.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I'm sure he did. And both of us have known that for a long time now, too. He simply chose... to bang his head on the past, straight-on.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Well, well. We said give us some peace and quiet to think on things...

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Not that either of us will ever have peace again.

a.text: A fowlbeast cries out. It is a unique cry, one that can only be heard before the coming of winter.
On hearing it, one thinks back to years past, to the fresh snow they tread upon and the frost on their weapons.
Though it was but a single snowflake silently falling into the abyss, they heard the long, roaring echo of the winter's northern winds.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: That said... sometimes I think, hey, even a good-for-nothing like me can do some good and rescue folks.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: So who exactly are these 'vast majority of folks' we're blaming here?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: When you look at it that way, maybe it's not all that disgraceful to be just an ordinary person.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Besides, he returned the sword to you.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...There's no place for such a sharp weapon in today's Kazimierz.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: He needn't have gone through the trouble.

a.text: Returning to their small huts in the corner of the village, the repatriated Infected workmen quietly walk past two neighbors who are discussing how to work together to collect the resources they need to make it through the winter.
Both the white haze of their breaths and the smoke from their kitchens slowly dissipate in the breeze.
They will never again wonder where they would spend the winter should the construction team arrive.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Speaking of which... Pinus Sylvestris asked me to pass on this letter of invitation to you.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...From Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: They may be a foreign company, but you're already pretty familiar with them, aren't you?

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: I know you aren't too interested in their particular business... but you should keep the letter.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: They actually helped us out a little when we pulled our little kidnapping stunt.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: The business permit I got from them definitely came in handy, not to mention the combat support from the young Pinus girls. I really owe them a huge favor.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Now, while you know I'd love for you to join me, alas, I get the impression you haven't changed your mind. So I might as well repay that favor now.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Besides, my guess is that their 'Doctor' must've told you something... About your brother and his wife.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Maybe a message from the Grand Knight? Perhaps Rossi's intention was to drop Margaret a hint, and in the end our favorite negotiator chose to pass the word on to you?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Even when speculating, you should know there are lines you shouldn't cross.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Hah, let me have my fun.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: So you plan to keep looking? Even though there hasn't been any news of them whatsoever?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I have no reason to abandon hope.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Even if that hope is baseless?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: It's more than enough.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...I was in the Grand Knight Territory for ten years, and all the hope I had those ten long years does not even compare to this hope.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Rather, only someone extremely childish would be satisfied with their life, this era... and themselves.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Well, ain't that the truth.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: Speaking of which, somehow I doubt you've written to Margaret lately.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: Do I need to? She's more than capable of taking responsibility for the trouble she invites.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: But what if the problems she runs into are ones you've dealt with before? Shouldn't you step up, as her guardian?

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: She should be following her own path, not mine.

steps.name: Toland
steps.text: So, where will you go now?

steps.name: Young Male Driver
steps.text: Excuse me, sirs?

steps.name: Young Male Driver
steps.text: Would you happen know where Dzwonek is at the moment? Is this the right way?

steps.name: Young Male Driver
steps.text: Huh? You don't know? I see, I guess I'll keep driving and find out.

steps.name: Little Girl's Voice
steps.text: I don't wanna sit in the car anymore—

steps.name: Young Male Driver
steps.text: We're almost there, sweetie. Just sit tight a little while longer. Daddy will get you a piccolo, okay?

steps.name: Young Male Driver
steps.text: You can't buy hand-crafted Leithanian instruments anywhere else.

a.text: He remembers practically every road there is, but not one of them points at a city that's always in motion, moving ever forward.
All roads have their destinations set in stone. What he seeks lies beyond any road.

steps.name: Młynar
steps.text: ...If a man is but a lost wanderer, what does it matter where he is, or where he's heading?
